categories.main_business_segments: Casey's operates a single reportable segment focused on convenience stores, offering a broad selection of merchandise, fuel, and other products and services. The company categorizes its revenue into three main product categories: fuel, grocery and general merchandise, and prepared food and dispensed beverage. Additionally, it manages a small dealer network for wholesale fuel supply, but this is not a separate operating segment.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Casey's leverages centralized distribution through three company-owned distribution centers and a company-operated delivery fleet to supply stores with groceries, general merchandise, and prepared foods. The company has installed full kitchens in nearly all stores (except GoodStop locations) to support its signature handmade pizza and other fresh food offerings. Technology investments include a digital rewards program, mobile app, and ongoing upgrades to IT systems for guest engagement and operational efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Casey's primarily serves individual consumers seeking convenience, with a focus on both small towns (often under 5,000 population) and larger communities. Key customer segments include commuters, local residents, and travelers purchasing fuel, prepared foods, snacks, beverages, and other convenience items. The company also supplies fuel on a wholesale basis to a network of dealer-operated stores.
categories.geographic_coverage: Casey's operates 2,521 convenience stores across 16 Midwestern and Southern states, with a concentration in Iowa, Missouri, and Illinois. The company’s footprint is primarily in the Midwest, with stores in both rural and urban areas, and distribution centers in Iowa, Indiana, and Missouri.
categories.supply_chain_position: Casey's operates downstream in the supply chain as a retailer, selling fuel, food, and merchandise directly to end consumers. It also manages some midstream activities through its self-distribution of fuel and goods to its stores and a small wholesale fuel dealer network.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Casey's strategic priorities include expanding its store footprint through new construction and acquisitions, enhancing the guest experience with digital engagement and loyalty programs, increasing private label product penetration, and investing in operational efficiencies. The company is also developing an electric vehicle charging strategy and expanding renewable fuel offerings to address evolving consumer preferences and environmental trends.
categories.revenue_model: Casey's generates revenue primarily through the retail sale of fuel (66% of total revenue), grocery and general merchandise, and prepared food and dispensed beverages. Additional revenue streams include car washes, lottery, and wholesale fuel sales to dealer-operated locations. The company also benefits from its Casey's Rewards loyalty program, which drives repeat purchases.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Casey's competes with national and regional convenience store chains (e.g., Quik Trip, Kwik Trip/Star, Kum & Go), grocery stores, drugstores, discount stores, supermarkets, and fuel stations. In smaller towns, competition is mainly from local stores, while in larger markets, it faces well-capitalized national and regional players. Casey's differentiates itself through its rural presence, foodservice offerings, and community focus.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended April 30, 2023, Casey's reported total revenue of $15.1 billion, with net income of $447 million and adjusted EBITDA of $959 million. The company grew its store count by 69 locations during the year and has demonstrated consistent revenue and earnings growth, driven by acquisitions, new store construction, and strong performance in prepared foods and private label products.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Casey's emphasizes its unique value proposition of offering freshly prepared foods—especially its signature handmade pizza—in a convenience store setting, often in underserved rural markets. The company differentiates itself through a broad product assortment, competitive pricing, community engagement, and a robust loyalty program, aiming to make guests' lives better every day and provide a one-stop shop for fuel, food, and convenience needs.
